_doc: Generated by experiment/playbook-completion/semantics/tools/trace_requirements.py from the ontology statements, src/trace_rules.json, src/trace_explicit.json, src/finding_classes.json and src/axioms_src.json. Do not edit; rerun the script. Each requirement lists its targets, the bases that gave them (detail maps basis -> targets) and its status; open requirements are also listed in 'open'. Rule-based traces are a mechanical classification; their measured precision is in data/trace_sample_review.json.
definition: A requirement is every ontology statement (experiment/playbook-completion/ontology/NN-*.md, Statements tables, all 19 modules 00-18) of kind B (business rule: what a user, tenant or operator can rely on), T (technical rule: how the product does it), I (invariant), X (refusal) or P (premise about IRIS, the driver or the operator). R (module roots), D (definitions, including local restatements) and Q (open questions, which name a human decision rather than state a rule) are not requirements. The ontology is the audit's one source-cited statement of intent for every module (literal 3.1 rule, 3,877 statements); the specs' FR-/SC- ids cover only some modules (no spec for vectors, interfaces or operations), and the ontology already cites the FR ids it restates in Source/Notes.
